texts.value: Alpha subunit of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), a key enzyme in nitric oxide (NO) signaling. sGC functions as a heterodimer consisting of one alpha and one beta subunit. It serves as the primary intracellular receptor for NO, which binds to a heme prosthetic group located on the beta subunit. Upon NO binding, sGC catalyzes the conversion of GTP into cyclic GMP (cGMP), thereby transmitting the NO signal into an ubiquitous intracellular second messenger
